pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin top-left, full-resolution pixels

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the moon region vs frame 0: max |dx| 0.5 px, |dy| 0.01 px over all 80 frames; moon limb x per row varies <= 2 px (mask noise)

objects.name: astronaut
objects.description: the only moving object: small white spacesuit figure with dark/gold visor, floating in black space to the right of the moon limb
objects.reference_point: cx, cy = centroid of the white-suit mask (stand-in for the pelvis/origin; at frame 0 it lies at the hip/pelvis region of the upright figure)
objects.direction: almost straight up the image (about 3 deg to the right of vertical), away from the moon's lower part

size_px.body_length_along_main_axis: 90.2-92.4 (median ~91.5); constant within noise, i.e. no apparent depth change

objects.orientation: main-axis angle (image coords, 90 = vertical) 94.7 deg at frame 0 -> 120.2 deg at frame 79: the body slowly tilts ~25 deg (head toward upper right, feet toward lower left); rotation eases in/out with the translation

objects.name: moon
objects.description: large grey cratered moon surface filling the left of the frame; curved limb on its right side; appears as a backdrop with straight horizontal cut edges at top and bottom
objects.limb: rightmost moon x: 840 at y=87, 998 at y=300, 1147 at y=540, 1274 at y=800, 1357 at y=992; circle fit to limb: centre (-1665.7, 2111.8), radius 3221.6 px (rms 1.4 px, only an arc is visible, so the radius is extrapolated)
objects.astronaut_gap_to_limb_px: radial gap centroid -> fitted limb circle: ~141 px at frame 0, ~292 px at frame 79

objects.name: stars
objects.description: a few faint 2-6 px white dots on the black sky, e.g. (1665,127), (1418,771), (1235,549), (1020,316)

events.note: centroid step 0.07 px at frame 1, 0.5-0.9 px at frames 2-4, growing

events.event: astronaut reaches peak pixel speed (plateau ~5.0-5.3 px/frame)

events.note: steps 0.5 px at frames 77-78, 0.04 px at frame 79; effectively stopped at the end

events.event: no bounces, impacts or contacts; direction stays nearly constant (upward)
